en: When working with Claude Code or with any AI
agents, it's a good idea to give them ways
of validating their work. That could be
automated tests. I'll get back to that. But
it can also be browser access, at least if
you're building a web app where they can
access a browser and test something. So for
example, here I got my development server up
and running. For me, it's running on port
3001. By default, it would be port 3000 and
I could now tell Claude code to test the
application it built. So I could say, test
the application you built using the
Playwright plugin or MCP, it's kind of the
same thing. Test all main features step by
step and ensure they work correctly.
And I also tell it that the application
server is already up and running and in my
case is running on port 3001. Playwright is
a tool that was initially built to help with
end-to-end testing of web applications and
that still is kind of its main purpose. But
with the rise of coding agents, it now is
It's also very popular for giving those
agents browser access so that they can
interactively explore a website and work
with it.
Now here, I'll not send this in plan mode,
but instead with accept edits on.
And what this should do now is use that
Playwright integration, which we added
through that plugin to then spin up a
browser window and navigate it on its own
and test the application on its own. So here
it's initially asking me for permission
since it wants to use that Playwright tool
and I don't want it to ask again, so I'm
fine with that.
And it did now open this browser. So this
browser window here was opened by Claude
Code and navigate to localhost:3001.
Now, since this is the first time it's using
this plugin, it's asking me for all kinds of
permissions related to Playwright. And
unless you enabled that mode where you
dangerously grant all permissions, you'll
have to initially allow them all step by
step.
But of course that will get better once it
used that plugin a bit more. And it can now
indeed navigate around and for example
navigate to this authentication page here.
Now it's asking for more permissions to fill
in that form field. So I'll allow that and
you see it filled in these form fields. And
as a next step, it will likely click this
button. Now it wants to take a snapshot of
the page so that it can look at it because
as mentioned before, Claude Code has image
vision and you can give it images, but it
can also of course, take a look at images
itself. It can also take a look at the
network requests that were sent or anything
like that. And as you can see, it now made
it to the dashboard and it will keep on
interacting with this site now creating a
new note. And that of course is a very
powerful capability since it allows Claude
Code to
test its UI changes and its website changes
